items.text: Beacon defines a compatibility registry schema with required fields for each compat, fallback, legacy, deprecated, or historical surface.
The registry covers all required compatibility-governance surfaces from the v1.4.11 baseline inventory.
Each registry entry records owner, surface category, reason, current replacement, default behavior, allowed version range, retirement route, and required evidence.
Command catalog entries are classified into current, support, advanced, labs, compat, deprecated, or internal layers.
Existing compat and deprecated command behavior remains available during this slice.
Default help, status, or next-route output does not promote compat or deprecated commands as normal current mainline routes.
Unregistered compatibility, fallback, deprecated, or legacy surfaces fail registry or catalog validation.
Tests prove QA legacy mirror, PRD legacy mirror, implement legacy loader, prototype legacy source, browser fallback, memory migration, and intent routing behavior are not changed by this slice.

state_machine: `inventory_available -> registry_required`: accepted by v1.4.11 Phase 2 scope decision.
`registry_required -> registry_defined`: implementation creates registry schema and entries.
`registry_defined -> catalog_layers_validated`: command catalog validation classifies current, support, advanced, labs, compat, deprecated, and internal entries.
`catalog_layers_validated -> behavior_change_ready_for_later_feature`: QA proves registry coverage and no behavior retirement.
`inventory_available -> behavior_retirement`: blocked because registry coverage does not exist yet.
`registry_defined -> command_removal`: blocked because this slice does not remove commands.
`registry_defined -> QA_legacy_policy_change`: blocked because QA mirror retirement is a later feature.
`registry_defined -> PRD_legacy_policy_change`: blocked because PRD mirror retirement is a later feature.
`catalog_layers_validated -> release_ready`: blocked unless implementation, QA, and release evidence close normally.

inputs_contract: conditionally required `prototype` when the feature has real UX/UI handoff
current gate / blocked reason / branch or execution governance context when present
decision_protocol: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
Block when frozen truth requires `change`, when cutover guardrails fail, or when a conditionally triggered prototype is still missing.
Keep `implement` as the only execution entry; `ask --execute` and support surfaces may route here but must not replace it.
Prefer explanation and routing logic in skill surface; keep final schema, contract, and gate writes in Python guardrails.
When dual-read or compatibility windows exist, fail closed on mismatch.
anti_inertia_notes: `implement` is not permission to rewrite requirement truth.
`goal`, task ledgers, or partial execution progress do not define completion truth.
If the feature needs UX/UI handoff and prototype is triggered, do not skip straight into coding.
Team/runtime internals stay internal unless the user explicitly asks for them.
`implement` cannot rewrite frozen truth or override gate truth by itself.
learning_notes: Reuse implementation learning to avoid repeated blocked paths or flaky cutovers.
Learning may shape route explanation and caution, but cannot override gate truth.
Downgrade stale learning instead of silently trusting it.
